transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-21 09:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (AE), Priya Raman (SE), Diego Morales (Solutions Eng) -- MerchantEdge: Samir Patel (CTO), Lina Gomez (Head of ML), Marcus Reid (Platform Eng), Aisha Khan (SecOps), Tom Boyle (Product)

Summary (auto): POC scope to validate integration approach for MerchantEdge customer support assistant; primary focus on throughput and latency under bursty e-commerce traffic and verifying structured output reliability for downstream order routing systems.

Topics: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, SDK vs OpenAI-compat endpoint, function calling, structured output schemas, security requirements.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): All right good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 50 minutes on the agenda to run through scope for the POC, benchmark expectations and the integration approach. Quick round robin intros?
[00:12] Samir (CTO): Hi all Samir here, CTO at MerchantEdge — we run the checkout and post-purchase support systems, interested in offloading first-line conversations to an LLM but with strict latency and reliability needs.
[00:25] Lina (Head of ML): Lina, I lead ML. We're prototyping NLU stacks but need inference that matches our SLA and plays well with our event-driven architecture.
[00:37] Jordan: Great. Priya and Diego from our side will lead the tech plan and benchmarks. Priya, quick intro?
[00:43] Priya (SE): Hey! Priya, inference eng. I'll map the benchmark matrix and run the initial tests. Happy to deep dive on latency knobs and the SDK integration path.
[00:52] Marcus (Platform): Marcus from platform. Big question for us is: can we use Redwood's OpenAI-compatible endpoints behind our API gateway or do we need to run the SDK in our infra? Network constraints and secrets management drive this.
[01:05] Priya: Short answer: both are supported. We typically recommend OpenAI-compatible endpoints for quick POCs, then move to SDK/private deployment for low-latency or residency. But we'll validate with benchmarks.
[01:20] Samir: Success criteria — what are reasonable numbers to target? p95 latency under 400ms and cost under $0.15 per 1k tokens for the pilot?
[01:33] Jordan: Those are good starter goals. Let's break down success criteria into three buckets: performance (latency/p95, p99), cost (cost per 1k tokens and cost per conversation), and functional quality (intent accuracy, structured field extraction F1).
[01:48] Lina: For structured output we absolutely need deterministic JSON with schema validation — we need to pipe extracted order numbers, refund reasons into our downstream systems without manual post-processing.
[01:58] Diego: We can use Redwood's structured output feature with strict schemas. Note: sometimes the transcriber shows 'schema enforcement' as optional, but we can run tests to measure failure rate. Also tool/function calling for calls to order-lookup microservice — we'll test roundtrip.
[02:15] Tom (Product): To be clear: if the model hallucinates an order ID, that's a deal breaker. Need guardrails + deterministic tooling or a human-in-the-loop fallback.
[02:28] Priya: Agreed, we'll include a hallucination rate metric in the benchmark sheet. We'll also test automatic re-query/verification via function calling: model returns order id, our function call runs lookup and validates.
[02:43] Aisha (SecOps): Quick security note — we need audit logs, KMS integration, and SSO for access. Also data retention policy must be clear for PII handling.
[02:55] Jordan: We'll share SOC2 docs and our KMS flow. For PII we can route through a tokenization step or promise ephemeral logs for the POC.
[03:10] Marcus: On workload sizing — our peak qps is around 120 req/s during sales events, with average sequence length 150 tokens and bursts up to 300 qps for short periods. Steady state closer to 25 qps.
[03:28] Priya: That's really helpful. For benchmarks we'll emulate both steady-state and burst profiles. Can you send a histogram of token lengths and inter-arrival times?
[03:36] Samir: Yes we'll export that.
[03:38] Jordan: We'll aim to run three benchmark stages: baseline (small sample), scale (up to 150 qps sustained) and burst (300 qps short). Each stage we'll capture p50/p95/p99, throughput, and cost.
[03:56] Lina: Also include accuracy tests: intent classification and entity extraction on our labelled set. We have 800 prompts and expected F1 > 0.88.
[04:07] Priya: Noted. For integration we discussed two routes: 1) OpenAI-compatible API calls using existing SDKs (fast) 2) Install Redwood SDK/inference client in your infra and call a private endpoint. Pros/cons?
[04:21] Jordan: Route 1 is fastest to get started — we spin up a sandbox project, give you keys. Route 2 better for lowest-latency and data residency, but needs network setup (VPC peering or Private Gateway) and slightly longer lead time.
[04:38] Marcus: Latency is sensitive — 400ms p95 target across our east-coast users. If the hosted API adds 80-120ms network overhead, that might push us over.
[04:50] Diego: We can test both. If the OpenAI-compat path misses the SLA by a small margin, we can evaluate Dedicated nodes in the same region. Also quantized model variants typically reduce latency by 20-30% at cost of minor accuracy changes.
[05:06] Samir: About function calling: we want the model to call our order-lookup function and then return structured output. Does Redwood support synchronous tool calling with enforced schema?
[05:18] Priya: Yes, we support tool/function calling and schema constraints. Implementation detail: you register an OpenAPI-like function descriptor; the model will emit a structured payload, Redwood can call your webhook, and you can set automatic verification steps. We'll prototype it in the POC.
[05:36] Lina: One caveat: our product needs nested structures for order and refund metadata — make sure the schema supports nested types and arrays.
[05:45] Diego: It does. We'll include nested schema tests in the structured-output benchmark. Also we'll measure failure modes where the model returns a near-miss field name.
[05:58] Tom: Who will own the code integration? Our eng can do the initial wiring but expect Redwood to provide example SDK code and a quickstart repo.
[06:08] Jordan: We'll provide a Git repo with SDK examples (node/python/go) and a dockerized test harness for traffic replay.
[06:17] Aisha: For security paperwork — we need SOC2, encryption details, contract addendum for data handling. Who sends those?
[06:24] Jordan: I'll send the compliance pack and a short summary of our KMS/HSM flow.
[06:30] Marcus: Network setup question: We prefer Private Gateway over VPC peering because our infra policy restricts peering. Is that supported?
[06:39] Priya: Yes, Private Gateway is supported. We'll ask for your egress IP ranges and set up the tunnel. We'll put steps in the runbook.
[06:49] Samir: Timeline — we were thinking a 6-week POC with three milestones: week 1-2 integration + baseline, week 3-4 scale benchmark and accuracy tuning, week 5-6 production pilot and handoff. Does that seem realistic?
[07:04] Priya: Totally realistic. We'll propose a detailed schedule in the benchmark matrix. If Dedicated provisioning needed, that can add 5-7 business days to the timeline depending on capacity.
[07:18] Jordan: Pricing — preliminary estimate for 6-week pilot with limited Dedicated burst capacity is in the email I will send. For hosted tests the cost will mostly be per-token during benchmark runs.
[07:29] Tom: What about rollback behavior if accuracy drops in production? We want canary traffic routing and automatic fallback to older model variant.
[07:37] Diego: Redwood supports rollout policies and automatic fallback. We'll include canary config in the playbook.
[07:44] Lina: One more thing — for evaluation metrics, can you capture token-level cost breakdown in the dashboard and also per-route latency?
[07:52] Priya: Yes token-level cost and per-route dashboards are part of Redwood Console. We'll give you an account view during the POC.
[08:00] Jordan: Ok let's recap action items and next steps. Priya will send benchmark template; Samir and Marcus will send traffic histogram and network constraints; Jordan will send compliance docs and pricing. We'll tentatively kick off May 4th.
[08:14] Samir: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[08:17] Jordan: Thanks all. We'll follow up with calendar invite for the infra deep dive.

(Transcript ends)
